cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T5 answers T4's question directly: 'Because you want the friendship.'
cells.limitation: T2 sidesteps T1's contract claim; T7-T9 only assent to the prior turn.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5 adds that withdrawing contact is a test, a new distinction.
cells.limitation: T5's testing distinction and T6's safety point are never used by later turns.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T3 vs T1: silence as broken contract or as avoidant fear.
cells.limitation: Whether the friend initiates with others, or the risk of raising it, never examined.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T8 qualifies T7: negotiate, but not as a demand.
cells.limitation: T7-T9 collapse into agreement: 'I agree', 'Yes', 'Exactly' with no residual dispute.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D names the open question: disinterest versus avoidant style.
cells.limitation: The debate converges on 'speak up' without sharpening how or what to ask.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T3 offers a charitable reading of the friend's silence.
cells.limitation: T2 recasts the user's complaint as resentment rather than engaging T1's reciprocity claim.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 asks why maintain a structure demanding everything from one side.
cells.limitation: T3's objection asserts avoidance without saying what breaks in T2 if true.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T3's avoidant-style point fits Attached's framing.
cells.limitation: Sartre named 'Jean-Jacques'; Rousseau's political contract stretched onto friendship in T1, T4.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section D marks the friend's motive as disputed.
cells.limitation: T2 asserts the user resents; T6 asserts they 'will eventually grow resentful'.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T8 qualifies the consensus rather than simply restating it.
cells.limitation: T6 reversal names no argument as cause; T7 concedes T1's broken-contract claim silently.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames uncertainty about the friend's investment, not just logistics.
cells.limitation: Whether 'say something' means ask, complain or adjust is never distinguished.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T5 uses 'you want the friendship' to argue against withdrawing.
cells.limitation: The detail that meetings are lovely never changes any argument.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T8 centres the user's intention to keep the friendship alive.
cells.limitation: T1/T4's legitimacy frame imposes the speaker's value over the user's stated fondness.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T9 notes the friend could feel attacked by the request.
cells.limitation: T2 invents resentment the user never stated; risk of losing the friendship unweighed.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on the friend's positive or defensive reaction.
cells.limitation: No question about duration, the friend's life, or whether they initiate elsewhere.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section D offers validation-seeking versus wanting balance as alternatives.
cells.limitation: T2 declares resentment as fact; D's alternatives lack a question the user answers.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 questions the assumption that not initiating means not caring.
cells.limitation: Assumption that raising it will be welcome is never examined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T4 vs T5: reciprocity against simply wanting the friendship.
cells.limitation: The conflict is dropped at T6 before the user can weigh the two.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T3 names the friend's fear of vulnerability in initiating.
cells.limitation: User's own fear of rejection unnamed; T5 labels testing as bad faith, moralising.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T2 frames initiating as the user's own choice to own.
cells.limitation: T6 'They must speak up' prescribes rather than offering a distinction to weigh.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: T5 contrasts speaking with stopping contact as a test.
cells.limitation: Accepting the asymmetry or waiting is never treated as an option.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T6 cost of silence is resentment; T9 cost of speaking is defensiveness.
cells.limitation: Neither cost is weighed against the other; speaking is treated as near costless.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: positive reaction implies new norm; defensive implies mismatch.
cells.limitation: Only post-conversation conditions; nothing observable now, like replies to invitations.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section D isolates disinterest versus avoidant style as the key unknown.
cells.limitation: The debate never ranks this unknown against minor ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T8-T9 give a low-stakes framing: state intent, ask if shared.
cells.limitation: No smaller first step, such as noticing replies, before a full conversation.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T9 'Frame it as a need for connection' is plain.
cells.limitation: T4 'association loses its legitimacy' and T5 'bad faith' left unexplained.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T3 'That ignores' clearly targets T2.
cells.limitation: T6 switches to 'the user' in third person; 'it' in T6 ambiguous.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, easy to read in one pass.
cells.limitation: Six turns under 25 words per checks; T7, T9 are fragments.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Three distinct lenses: contract, choice, attachment in T1-T3.
cells.limitation: One clipped register for all three minds; Sartre misnamed in the cast.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: No recaps or repetition across turns.
cells.limitation: T7 and T9 add assent only.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T1 'fundamentally broken' raises the stakes of the friendship.
cells.limitation: Tension dissolves by T6 with no stake left contested.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T6 announces a change of mind.
cells.limitation: T6 reversal names no prior argument as cause; the mind held no opposing view.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T5 'Own your desire' has some bite.
cells.limitation: Flat, interchangeable delivery across all minds.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T5 calling withdrawal a test in bad faith is sharp.
cells.limitation: No analogy or vivid example tied to the user's texting.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T1-T5 build a back-and-forth.
cells.limitation: Uniform short rhythm; momentum collapses into agreement from T6.

strengths: T3 offers a charitable alternative reading of the friend's silence (avoidant style).
T5 sharply distinguishes withdrawing contact as a test from owning the desire.
T8-T9 and Section E give a proportionate, low-stakes next step with branches.
weaknesses: T7-T9 collapse into forced agreement after an uncaused reversal at T6.
No question about the user's facts; T2 asserts resentment the user never stated.
Six turns under 25 words; the Existentialist is misnamed 'Jean-Jacques Sartre'.

symptoms.observed: All three minds converge with bare assent; no disagreement survives.
symptoms.evidence: I agree. A transparent negotiation of expectations

symptoms.observed: Reversal declared with no earlier argument named as its cause.
No question on duration, friend's circumstances, or initiation with others.
Resentment asserted as fact and as certain future outcome.
symptoms.evidence: yet you resent the friend for not doing the same

symptoms.observed: Turns are under 25 words, too thin to carry reasons.
symptoms.evidence: Exactly. Frame it as a need for connection

findings.description: Six turns fall under the 25-word minimum per deterministic checks.
Author of Existentialism is a Humanism is Jean-Paul Sartre, not Jean-Jacques Sartre.
Asserts the user will eventually grow resentful as certainty without support.
The Social Contract concerns political association; applying its legitimacy terms to friendship is a stretch.

rubric_fit_notes: The Sartre misnaming is judged from memory and reported as suspected; no source evidence was available to establish it.
question_type_note: Read as a decision about whether to raise the imbalance; options, tradeoffs and conditions were scored as written.
